proposals.evidence: DEDR 3675 directly gives Gondi nil-, Kota nil-/nin- and Kurukh ijnā stand. Source cognacy identifies the same article; survey Kota ninnatukə and Kurukh ijjna retain their inflection and consonant transcription rather than being rewritten as dictionary stems. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 561 documents Kannada ugur, Kodagu oy, Gondi gōr, Kurukh orox, Kuwi gōru with plural gōrka, Malto orgu and Toda ǖr as the nail/claw family. Survey final vowels and plural-looking material remain unchanged. Badaga ugilə is a comparative extension explicitly described as a look-alike in the source; Kodagu voyi and Toda yūr retain their initial glide/transcription differences. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5024 directly gives Tamil/Malayalam mūkku, Kota mūk, Kodagu mūkï, Kurukh muĩ and Parji muvāḍ nose. Source annotations identify this article. Badaga, Betta Kurumba and Ravula mūkə/mūkkə are comparative extensions to lects not listed there; no exact DEDR attestation is claimed for them. Parji nasal-vowel spelling muvãḍ is preserved. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 474 explicitly documents Kannada eraḍu, Kodagu daṇḍï, Kota eyḏ, Kurukh irb (two persons), Kuwi rindi, Malayalam raṇṭu, Parji adjectival ir, Tamil reṇṭu and Toda ēḍ. The survey cognacy annotations independently identify the article. Final vowels and the Kurukh personal versus Parji adjectival use are retained; no grammatical category is silently added to the generic survey gloss two. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 1931 gives Kurukh xẽs blood, xẽso red/blood and Malto qéso red. Source cognacy identifies this article. Survey Kurukh kʰēns/kheso retain their transcription of frication/nasality; Malto ēso is a comparative proposal whose missing initial q- remains visible for review, not silently repaired. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
